### Scoped grant ownership across workflow and governance commits

Two workers can observe the same reservation before either journals the workflow grant.
Releasing by holder on a failed append let the losing worker transfer the only ticket to
a queued rival while the winner's checkpoint still showed it held. The durable lease
occurrence therefore owns the ticket across attempts. An append conflict leaves it in
place for the winner or a replacement. A committed closure before activation authorizes compensation, and
the governance receipt supplies the ticket identity if workflow publication must be retried.
Direct admission and FIFO promotion validate the owning checkpoint in the governance write
so a committed cancellation also fences a worker that read eligibility earlier.
[DR-038](../specs/16-requirements-durable-driver.md#dr-038-scoped-durable-lease-occurrences-are-committed-ancestry-safe-state-machines)
· [Original failure and regression evidence](../../verification/tla/durable-resource-grant/README.md)

Scoped admission and queued promotion additionally require
`ICheckpointGuardedResourceGovernanceStore.AppendIfCurrentAsync`. The host supplies the
owner checkpoint versions it used to admit those occurrences. The provider checks every
version in the same transaction as the governance append. A changed or missing owner
checkpoint returns a conflict so the host can re-evaluate eligibility. Wrapped providers
forward this capability. An implementation without it cannot issue new scoped reservations.

no-ops. On both SQL providers, queue a rival for the last unit, let A commit the shared
  grant, and force B's append to lose. While A holds the lease, its original ticket and
  provider generation remain and the rival stays queued. After a host stops, verify adoption
  of a live reservation or exact compensation of a closed occurrence. If governance already
  transferred capacity, replay records one workflow release and preserves the successor ticket.
  [MG-064/065, DR-038, DR-AC-036] [Model and provider schedules](../../verification/tla/durable-resource-grant/README.md)

The durable lease occurrence owns the reservation across worker attempts. When two workers
observe the same ticket and only one workflow append commits, the losing append SHALL leave
the ticket and its provider generation with the occurrence. This holds before and after
activation. A replacement driving a still-pending occurrence can adopt that same ticket.
If the occurrence closes before activation, recovery SHALL use the governance receipt to
publish one matching release, including its exact tickets or the empty set for cancellation
before grant. Replaying that receipt SHALL preserve any queued successor's transferred ticket.

edits.before: per-workflow streams does not satisfy v1 durable leasing.
edits.after:
per-workflow streams does not satisfy v1 durable leasing. Scoped grant and FIFO promotion use
the provider-facing `ICheckpointGuardedResourceGovernanceStore` extension. It additionally
conditions the same governance append on the current versions of the admitted owners'
workflow checkpoints. Cancellation requests advance the owner checkpoint in their commit.
